lesson: The cutoff commutator of a Hecke dilation is kernel-free and its range is a whole window, so any form built on it is the cutoff (Weil) form restricted to a window. That form separates kernels by the functional equation and by the height of the lowest off-line zero, not by the Euler product: non-multiplicative DH passes, completely multiplicative Liouville fails at 1e-8. The count of negative directions is set by test-space dimension, not by P.
